extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in differential geometry and geometric analysis (Ricci flow)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and constructions for analyzing long-time/nonsingular normalized Ricci flows on compact 3-manifolds: classification by scalar curvature minimum, taking noncollapsing limits, producing persistent hyperbolic pieces via harmonic parametrizations, and proving incompressibility of boundary tori via minimal-surface/area estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: C^∞ convergence on compact sets (topology via d_C^k(K))
rubrics_metrics.description: Convergence of maps F: M -> N is defined by the metrics d_{C^k}(K) on compact sets K: use k-jet spaces J^kM, J^kN and a k-jet distance d_{C^k(K)}(F,G) = d_{B J^k K}(J^kF, J^kG); convergence in d_{C^k}(K) for all k and all compact K defines C^∞ convergence on compact sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the precise topology used when taking pointed limits of manifolds / marked manifolds: control of all derivatives on every compact subset (C^∞_loc). The text gives the k-jet description and the metric used to measure closeness of maps on a compact core.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mostow-type rigidity via C^q closeness on compact core (Lemma 5.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any complete noncompact finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold H with metric h, there exists a compact K (a truncated core) so that for any integer k and ε>0, there exist q and δ>0 with: if F is a diffeomorphism from H to another finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold \tilde H (with no fewer cusps) and ||F^*\tilde h - h||_{C^q(K)} < δ, then there exists an isometry I of H with d_{C^k(K)}(F, I) < ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Margulis lemma to choose a compact core K (cut off cusps). The lemma is used to promote small C^q perturbations of the metric (on the core) into an actual isometry up to small C^k error; it justifies identifying a limit almost-isometry with an actual isometry when the core metrics are close.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of nearby harmonic diffeomorphism (Lemma 5.3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (X,g) is compact with strictly negative Ricci curvature and strictly concave boundary, then there exist integers l0 and for small ε0>0: for any l ≥ l0 and sufficiently small metric perturbation ||\tilde g - g||_{C^q(X)} ≤ δ, there is a unique diffeomorphism F of X to itself with (a) F:(X,g)->(X,\tilde g) harmonic, (b) F maps ∂X to ∂X and satisfies the free-boundary condition (normal derivative at boundary is normal to boundary), and (c) d_{C^l(X)}(F, Id) < ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by mapping the space of maps taking boundary to itself and applying the inverse function theorem. The linearized operator is an isomorphism because the kernel of the linear elliptic boundary problem (∆V + Ric(V) =0, boundary conditions) is trivial when Ric<0 and the second fundamental form II<0. This lemma gives control and uniqueness of harmonic parametrizations near the identity under small metric perturbations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinching estimate controlling negative sectional curvatures (Theorem 5.3.2 referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pinching inequality bounds the negative eigenvalue ˜ν of the curvature operator in terms of the scalar curvature ˜R and time: roughly ˜ν ≥ -(˜R/3)[log(-˜ν) + log(1+t) + C] (whenever ˜ν<0), so when the unnormalized curvature becomes large, negative curvatures are much smaller in magnitude than positive ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly to conclude that after rescaling (normalized flow) negative sectional curvatures go to zero while positive ones may remain finite; this is the technical core behind showing limits have nonnegative sectional curvature and ultimately constant sectional curvature in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of nonsingular normalized Ricci flows by behavior of R_min(t)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide noncollapsing nonsingular solutions of the normalized Ricci flow into three cases according to R_min(t)=min_x R(x,t): (1) R_min(t)>0 for some t>0; (2) R_min(t) ≤ 0 for all t and lim_{t→∞} R_min(t)=0; (3) R_min(t)<0 for all t and lim_{t→∞} R_min(t)=c<0 (in particular → -6 in context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This trichotomy organizes the global long-time analysis and determines the type of geometric limits obtainable (positive constant curvature, flat / product, or hyperbolic pieces). The monotonicity and maximum principle for R_min are used to justify the cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for obtaining noncollapsing limits with nonnegative sectional curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: In Cases (1) and (2) one shows a noncollapsing limit has nonnegative sectional curvature by combining pinching estimates, behavior of the unnormalized flow (blow-up or global existence), and volume/normalization scaling arguments: when scaling factors go to infinity negative curvatures rescale to zero; when normalized scalar curvature is bounded, pinching forces negative eigenvalues → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives separate subcases (2.1–2.3) based on volume behavior of the unnormalized flow and explains how each leads to a noncollapsing limit with nonnegative sectional curvature. Use the pinching inequality and control of scaling/normalization to check limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of persistent hyperbolic pieces via harmonic parametrizations
rubrics_metrics.description: To exhibit persistent hyperbolic pieces (Theorem 5.3.4(ii)), pick a hyperbolic limit H and truncate each cusp at small area a to obtain a compact core H_a. Choose l0, ε0 (Lemma 5.3.8) and q0, δ0 (Lemma 5.3.7). For a sequence of times t_k where (M,g(t_k),p_k) → (H,h,p), produce harmonic diffeomorphisms F_k : H_a → M whose pullback metrics satisfy ||F_k^* g(t_k) - h||_{C^{q}(H_a)} < δ. Then continue F_k(t) in time as long as the C^q(H_a) pullback closeness < δ; at least one such piece persists for all large times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit step-by-step recipe: truncate cusps, pick parameters from the two lemmas, perturb maps to be harmonic with free-boundary condition, and use implicit function theorem + compactness to extend in time; control of C^q-norm ensures the map remains close to an isometry and hence the hyperbolic geometry persists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/continuation criterion for harmonic parametrizations (stopping rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given harmonic diffeomorphisms F_k(t) from H_a into (M,g(t)) defined for t in [t_k, ω_k) and satisfying ||F_k^*(t) g(t) - h||_{C^q(H_a)} < δ, they can be continued forward in time as long as this C^q(H_a) norm stays strictly below δ; the maximal extension time ω_k either is +∞ or the norm reaches δ at t = ω_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a clear quantitative continuation/stopping criterion: monitor the pullback C^q-norm and use elliptic regularity + inverse function theorem to extend while the metric closeness remains below the threshold δ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Margulis lemma and choice of compact core via l^{-1}([0, ε0])
rubrics_metrics.description: Define l(x) = length of shortest non-contractible loop at x. For small ε0 (less than half the minimal closed geodesic length on tubes), the set l^{-1}([0,ε0]) has finitely many components, each a cusp or tube; truncating beyond these components yields a compact core K0 whose boundary consists of flat tori with constant mean curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the method to select the compact region K used in Mostow-type rigidity and in truncating cusps for harmonic parametrizations; choose ε0 so that only actual cusp regions are cut off, not tubes bounding solid tori.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompressibility criterion for boundary tori via minimal-disk area evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove boundary tori of a persistent hyperbolic piece are incompressible: assume a torus T compresses, choose an embedded least-area disk D (normal to boundary) bounding a primitive loop; let A(t) be its area. Compute dA/dt under normalized Ricci flow and derive an inequality (using Gauss, Gauss-Bonnet, pinching and closeness to hyperbolic geometry) that forces A'(t) ≤ c1 L - c2 A - 2π with constants giving a strictly negative bound (area decreases at rate bounded away from zero), contradicting minimality for large times; hence π1(T) injects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key ingredients: formula for ∂_t dσ on disk (projection of Ricci tensor), Gauss equation expressing K in terms of ambient curvature and second fundamental form, Gauss–Bonnet for disk, control of boundary geodesic curvature and normal velocity because the region is arbitrarily close to hyperbolic. The argument turns geometric/topological compression into a quantitative area-decreasing contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area-derivative estimate using curvature decomposition and Gauss–Bonnet (inequalities (5.3.12) and (5.3.13))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a minimal bounding disk at time t0, one has dA/dt ≤ ∫_{disk}((2/3)r - (1/2)R) dσ - ∫_{disk} K dσ + ∫_{∂disk} k ds + ∫_{∂disk} N ds, and using Gauss–Bonnet (∫_disk K dσ + ∫_{∂disk} k ds = 2π) and closeness to hyperbolic geometry this yields an explicit upper bound of the form dA/dt ≤ (1+2ε0)L - (1-ε0)A - 2π ≤ (1+2ε0)L - (1-ε0)A - 2π for small ε0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit inequality quantifies how area evolves under the normalized flow and is central to the incompressibility argument. It combines scalar curvature asymptotics (r and R tending to -6), control of boundary curvature and boundary motion (N) due to near-hyperbolic geometry, and the Gauss–Bonnet topological term 2π.
